skills.trigger: When evaluating a chest radiograph for cystic or cavitary lung lesions to determine the specific lobar location and laterality.
steps: Identify the side of the abnormality by locating the cardiac silhouette and gastric bubble; opacities behind the heart shadow on the left indicate a retrocardiac/left lower lobe location.

Distinguish between upper and lower lobes by assessing vertical position relative to the hilum and diaphragm; lower lobe lesions typically project over the lower thorax and may be partially obscured by the heart.

Differentiate left from right lower lobe pathology by noting that right lower lobe lesions usually silhouette the right hemidiaphragm, whereas left lower lobe lesions appear as retrocardiac densities.

skills.trigger: When correlating the anatomical location of cystic lung lesions with the likely subtype of pulmonary sequestration and its vascular supply.
steps: Recognize that cystic or cavitary opacities in the lower lobes (especially the left) are characteristic of intralobar pulmonary sequestration.
Associate intralobar sequestration with a systemic arterial supply arising from the thoracic or abdominal aorta, distinguishing it from extralobar sequestration which may have different associations.
Exclude diagnoses suggesting pulmonary artery supply or upper lobe predominance when the imaging shows classic lower lobe cystic changes consistent with intralobar sequestration.
